title: Bladder instillation
what: The doctor puts medicine straight into the bladder through a thin catheter. It works on the bladder wall from the inside.
why: For chronic bladder inflammation, some types of bladder pain, and to prevent recurrence after treatment of bladder tumors.
duration: the procedure usually takes 10 to 15 minutes; the medicine stays in the bladder for 30 minutes to 2 hours, as your doctor says
tell_doctor: If you have a fever, pain, or blood in your urine right now
Allergies, including to latex and numbing gels

prepare.title: Drinking
prepare.text: You are usually asked to drink less for a few hours before, so the medicine stays in longer. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Course
prepare.text: It is usually a course of several sessions. Check the schedule.

steps: You pee and lie on your back on the couch
The genital area is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing gel is put into the urethra
The medicine is poured in through the catheter
The catheter is removed, and the medicine stays in the bladder for the time your doctor says
feel: An unpleasant feeling as the catheter goes in
An urge to pee while the medicine is in
after: After that, drink more water, unless your doctor says otherwise
Burning and frequent urges on the first day can happen
Some medicines need special hygiene afterward. Your doctor will explain
red_flags: A lot of blood in your urine

faq.a: Usually not. The catheter is thin, and a numbing gel is used. It can be unpleasant.
Usually a course of several. Your doctor will decide how many.

reminders.text: Bladder instillation soon. You are usually asked to drink less for a few hours. Pee before the procedure.
